solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Making a comeback, arrival constrained by dumb mistake (7)

indicatorNotes.Making a comeback: coming back means running the letters the other way
indicatorNotes.constrained by: the arrival is held inside the word for dumb

blocks.note: dumb = unable to speak
arr. is the abbreviation printed on timetables for arrival

annotation.surface: A sports star's comeback is spoiled when a silly blunder holds up their return.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dumb' is not about silence in the story but a source of letters, and 'Making a comeback' is the step applied last, after the arrival is tucked in.
annotation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error, especially one listed for correction in a printed book.

entries.clue: State test incorporating two separate elements (7)

indicatorNotes.incorporating: the test takes the elements into its body

blocks.note: an exam is a test
Cl (chlorine) and I (iodine), chemical symbols placed at two separate points

annotation.surface: A test paper on chemistry in which two distinct elements appear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Separate' is the key: the two elements do not go into the test side by side but at two different points, so the chlorine and iodine are split by a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to state something, typically loudly or suddenly.

entries.clue: Cheerful alternative, but not very advanced (5)

indicatorNotes.but not: the word loses the letters for very and advanced

blocks.note: a variant is an alternative version
V = very, A = advanced; both removed from the front

annotation.surface: Someone offers a more upbeat option that is only modestly forward-thinking.
annotation.walkthrough: RIANT is a rare literary word, borrowed from French, meaning smiling or cheerful.
annotation.definitionFit: Riant means laughing or cheerful, from the French rire, to laugh.

entries.clue: Lie about second-class syllabus (5)

indicatorNotes.about: the lie goes around the letter

blocks.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales
B is second class, after A

annotation.surface: A complaint that someone is misrepresenting a course of study as second-rate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lie' wants to be a verb; here it is the noun, a fib.
annotation.definitionFit: A table, as in a schedule or timetable of topics, can set out what a course covers.

entries.clue: Prima ballerina’s distinction at an end according to gossip (7)

indicatorNotes.according to gossip: gossip is talk, so the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a mark of distinction
over = finished; spoken in a British accent it sounds like OVA

annotation.surface: Talk has it that a great dancer's celebrated career is finished.
annotation.walkthrough: Alicia Markova was a celebrated English prima ballerina. The sound match needs a non-rhotic accent, where the final R of OVER is silent.
annotation.definitionFit: Dame Alicia Markova was one of the great prima ballerinas of the twentieth century.

entries.clue: Characteristic of one pair of diamonds held by one pair of spades (7)

blocks.note: D = diamonds, twice
ONE taken as written, then S = spades twice; ONE holds the DD

annotation.surface: A card player describes a hand in which a pair of diamonds sits with a pair of spades.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' appears twice with different jobs: the first belongs to the definition, since the number one is odd; the second is the literal word that holds DD.
annotation.definitionFit: One is an odd number, so oddness is one of its defining properties.

entries.clue: Greasy member putting down one adult source of games? (7)

indicatorNotes.putting down: in a down entry, moving the I further down the word

blocks.note: OILY, with its I moved down past the member
an MP is a Member of Parliament
the I from OILY, put down below MP
A = adult, the film rating

annotation.surface: An oily limb that turns out to be where some games come from.
annotation.walkthrough: OILY plus MP gives OILYMP; the I is then dropped lower to give OLYMPI, and A finishes it. Olympia in Greece was the site of the ancient Olympic Games.
annotation.definitionFit: The Olympic Games take their name from Olympia, where they were held in ancient Greece.

entries.clue: Extremely loud engine DAF redesigned (9)

indicatorNotes.redesigned: the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A lorry maker's reworked engine turns out to be ear-splitting.
annotation.walkthrough: DAF is a Dutch truck maker, which makes the surface about vehicles; the capitals are there to hide that the name is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Deafening describes a noise loud enough to make you temporarily deaf.

entries.clue: Base, drunk Heather reveals secrets to a few (9)

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
a sot is a drunkard
Erica is the botanical name for heather

annotation.surface: A low, tipsy woman called Heather lets confidential things slip to a select group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the noun SOT. Heather is capitalised to pass as a woman's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Esoterica are items or knowledge meant for, or understood by, only a small inner circle.

entries.clue: Bone needs hard lump shaved (7)

indicatorNotes.shaved: trimmed at both edges, losing its outer letters

blocks.note: stern = hard, severe
LUMP without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A bone with a hard lump on it needs smoothing down.
annotation.walkthrough: Here the outer letters are the ones thrown away, and the middle UM is kept.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sternum is the anatomist's name for the flat breastbone in the chest.

entries.clue: Clubs promoted Chuck, maybe for something with saucy connotations? (9)

indicatorNotes.maybe: Chuck is one example of a Berry

blocks.note: C = clubs, the card suit
ran = promoted, as a campaign or a candidate
Chuck Berry, the rock and roll pioneer

annotation.surface: Nightclubs pushed a rock star's songs, perhaps for their suggestive lyrics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests innuendo, but cranberry sauce is the connection. 'Chuck' looks like a verb meaning throw; it is Chuck Berry.
annotation.definitionFit: Cranberry is best known as the sauce served with turkey, hence its saucy associations.

entries.clue: Stay over when daughter’s ousted Victor (5)

indicatorNotes.’s ousted: the daughter has pushed out Victor and taken his place

blocks.note: above = over
D = daughter
V is Victor in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A father sleeps over at his daughter's house after she threw out a man named Victor.
annotation.walkthrough: D replaces the V in ABOVE. 'Stay' looks like a verb, but the answer is the noun: an abode is a stay, a place of residence.
annotation.definitionFit: An abode is a place where one stays or lives; the old sense of abide is to stay.

entries.clue: Style shown by TV duo, the first having a change of heart when given Oscar (3,4)

indicatorNotes.having a change of heart: the middle letter of the first name is swapped
indicatorNotes.when given: something given is handed over and added, so the O is tacked on at the end

blocks.clueFragment: TV duo, the first having a change of heart
blocks.note: ANT of Ant and Dec, with its middle N changed to R
the second of Ant and Dec
O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A TV double act's taste in design, with one of them changing his mind after winning an Oscar.
annotation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV presenting pair. 'Change of heart' is the key: ANT's heart, N, becomes R.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the geometric look of 1920s and 1930s design is one named style among many.

entries.clue: Fantastic entrée after a drop of Penderyn, twelve years old? (3-4)

indicatorNotes.Fantastic: wildly imagined, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.after: the rearranged word follows the P
indicatorNotes.a drop of: just the first bit of the whisky

blocks.note: the first letter of Penderyn
ENTREE rearranged

annotation.surface: A superb starter served after a dram of whisky aged twelve years.
annotation.walkthrough: Penderyn is a Welsh whisky, and 'twelve years old' reads as a whisky's age statement. It is really a child just short of the teens.
annotation.definitionFit: At twelve a child is a pre-teen, just below thirteen; the question mark flags the whisky pun.

entries.clue: Spanish woman embraces male compatriot in grass (9)

indicatorNotes.embraces: Maria holds Juan in her arms

blocks.note: a typical Spanish woman's name
a typical Spanish man's name

annotation.surface: A Spanish woman hugs a fellow Spaniard on a lawn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In grass' seems to set the scene on a lawn; grass is the slang definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: the dried leafy drug has long gone by the street name grass.

entries.clue: Ascent overwhelming American – that guy’s gonna cause trouble (5,4)

blocks.note: a rise is an ascent
A = American
HE'LL = he will, that guy is going to

annotation.surface: A climb swamping an American, and some bloke is about to kick up a fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: The chatty 'that guy's gonna' is a spelled-out contraction: he will, HE'LL.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: kicking up a loud, riotous fuss is making trouble in its noisiest form.

entries.clue: Recklessly went in front of Lincoln and Ford et al? (9)

annotation.definition: Recklessly went in front of Lincoln and Ford et al?

blocks.note: the surface reading is a line-up of US presidents, Abraham Lincoln and Gerald Ford among them
the setter means the car makes Lincoln and Ford: stepping carelessly out in front of traffic

annotation.surface: Someone rashly stood before two American presidents and their colleagues.
annotation.walkthrough: Lincoln and Ford read as US presidents, but they are car makes. Stepping carelessly across a road in front of cars is jaywalking.
annotation.definitionFit: To jaywalk is to cross a road recklessly, ignoring the traffic and the crossings.

entries.clue: Documents island dialect (5)

blocks.note: ID = identity documents
IOM = Isle of Man

annotation.surface: Someone records the local speech of an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Documents' looks like a verb; it is the noun giving ID. The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom is the particular language or dialect of a people or place.

entries.clue: Cleaner fastidiously scrubbing recycled tin (5)

indicatorNotes.scrubbing: rubbing out letters from the word
indicatorNotes.recycled: the letters of TIN turn up in another order

blocks.note: daintily = fussily, fastidiously
TIN rearranged, removed from DAINTILY

annotation.surface: A cleaner meticulously scouring a used can.
annotation.walkthrough: A daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day. The letters removed are not in the order TIN, which is why 'recycled' is there.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain a daily is a domestic cleaner who comes in by the day.

entries.clue: Denies connection with police officers gobbling spread (7)

indicatorNotes.gobbling: the officers eat up the spread

blocks.note: DIs = detective inspectors
seed is sown, spread over the field

annotation.surface: Suspects deny links to police officers who were greedily eating a buffet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spread' tempts as a meal to gobble; it is the past participle of sow.
annotation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to deny any connection with them.

entries.clue: Send a message to us (9)

blocks.note: the verb for sending word down a wire in Morse, or signalling something in advance
the newspaper speaking of itself, as the paper this puzzle ran in

annotation.surface: A plain request to get in touch with the people writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Us' is the newspaper speaking: this puzzle appeared in the Daily Telegraph.
annotation.definitionFit: To telegraph is to send a message by telegram; the Telegraph is the paper printing the clue.

entries.clue: Boring outside broadcast (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: sown far and wide, so scattered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A dull outside broadcast from a TV crew on location.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcast' is a fixed TV phrase, which hides that 'broadcast' is working on 'outside'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that drags on so long it wears you out is dull.

entries.clue: Circular feature of plant … (7)

blocks.note: the noun: a printed handout delivered to many homes
the botanist's word for each small leaf-like division of a compound leaf

annotation.surface: A curved part of a plant, the thought trailing on into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, a printed handout. The dots link this clue with 20 down, whose answer is also a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed circular, and also one of the small divisions of a compound leaf.

entries.clue: … one that’s straight up, though not large (7)

annotation.definitionNote: 'one' stands for a plant, carried over from 19 down

indicatorNotes.though not: the word is taken without the L

blocks.note: 'straight up' is British slang for honestly
L = large, removed

annotation.surface: Continuing 19 down: an upright plant, though not a big one.
annotation.walkthrough: The dots make 'one' mean a plant from the previous clue. Honesty is a garden plant with flat, papery, coin-shaped seed pods.
annotation.definitionFit: Honesty (Lunaria) is a garden plant grown for its silvery disc-shaped seed pods.

entries.clue: Tricky situation difficult when hotel’s sacked sommelier? (7)

indicatorNotes.’s sacked: the hotel letter is dismissed from the word

blocks.note: to be in a stew is to be in a fix
hard = difficult
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet, removed from HARD

annotation.surface: An awkward moment at a hotel after the wine waiter is fired.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a sommelier is a wine steward.
annotation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a wine steward, the restaurant staff member in charge of wine.

entries.clue: Unknown detective plugs articles about lost people (7)

indicatorNotes.plugs: the unknown and the detective fill a gap between the articles

blocks.note: A and AN, both forms of the indefinite article, which open to take the plug
z is an unknown in algebra
tec is slang for detective

annotation.surface: An unidentified sleuth promotes stories about people who went missing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plugs' reads as advertising; it means filling a hole. The Aztecs are a lost civilisation, overthrown by the Spanish in the 1520s.
annotation.definitionFit: Aztecan means relating to the Aztecs, a people whose empire vanished after the Spanish conquest.

entries.clue: Covering combined forces that move round without resistance (5)

indicatorNotes.without: the resistance letter is left out

blocks.note: torque is a turning force
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, removed

annotation.surface: Allied troops on the move form a protective shield without meeting opposition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Combined forces' reads as a military alliance; in physics torque is the combined effect of forces causing rotation.
annotation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, most familiar as a chef's tall white hat.

entries.clue: Stopping for last game holds up church service? (5)

indicatorNotes.Stopping: stopping a word at both ends cuts off its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.holds up: in a down entry, the game sits below and supports the church

blocks.note: CH = church
a last game is a FINAL; stopped at both ends it leaves INA

annotation.surface: Someone skipping the last round of play is keeping the congregation waiting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Church service' reads as a single idea, but the service is a dinner service. The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: China is porcelain tableware, and a set of it is a dinner or tea service.

entries.clue: Republican blocks unconvincing cause (5)

indicatorNotes.blocks: the Republican sits in the middle, blocking the way

blocks.note: a weak argument is unconvincing
R = Republican

annotation.surface: A Republican politician obstructs a feeble campaign.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cause' looks like a noun, a campaign; it is the verb, as in wreak havoc.
annotation.definitionFit: A collocation: this is the verb that goes with havoc or damage, meaning to inflict it.

entries.clue: Censures half of rest after old boy left with nothing (9)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
L = left
O = zero, nothing
the first half of QUIESCENCE, rest

annotation.surface: Criticism for taking only half a break after a former pupil walked out empty-handed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half of rest' needs the ten-letter word QUIESCENCE, not REST itself; its first five letters are taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Obloquy is strong public censure or abuse; obloquies are instances of it.

entries.clue: Slash hard bits from Unfinished Symphony (7)

indicatorNotes.bits from: just the first pieces of each word are taken

blocks.note: solid = hard
the first letters of Unfinished and Symphony

annotation.surface: Cut the difficult passages from Schubert's Unfinished Symphony.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slash' reads as a command to cut; it is the name of the / symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: A solidus is the oblique stroke /, also called a slash.

entries.clue: Trim back, cutting your old treatment (7)

indicatorNotes.back: the letters run the other way
indicatorNotes.cutting: the reversed word cuts into the old possessive

blocks.note: thy = your, in old English
PARE (trim) reversed

annotation.surface: A barber's instruction to trim the back, then a remark on someone's old-fashioned beauty treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trim back' reads as a haircut instruction; 'back' is the reversal signal applied to PARE.
annotation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal or relieve a disorder.
